Fig. 7: Measured on-board power during a single Edge–Cloud inference cycle (supply voltage 11.7 V, sampled frameby-frame from the DC power supply panel). Four operating regimes are visible: boot (rising from 0 to 7.6 W), NPU initialization (holding at 8.775 W), a peak inference burst reaching 11.85 W as the latent is transmitted to the cloud and decaying to 10.97 W (envelope width 3.21 s, matching the mean NPU encoding time of Table VI), and a cooldown back to 7.6 W. Subtracting the 7.6-W idle baseline, the NPU-attributable energy obtained by integrating (P (t)− Pidle) over the burst is 11.27 J.
Fig. 4: Progressive transmission with semantic quality-based control. The initial transmission of textual input is omitted in this diagram for simplicity.

Fig. 6: Measured on-board power during a single Full-Edge inference cycle, using the same supply, sampling, and power levels as Fig. 7. Two consecutive compute bursts are visible, each sharing the same envelope shape (rise– hold–decay–drop) as the single burst in Fig. 7: a first burst peaking at 11.85 W for the NPU vision encode (envelope width 3.20 s, matching Table IV) and a second slightly longer burst at the same peak for the auto-regressive LLM decode (envelope width 3.46 s, matching Table IV). The transition between the two bursts is a momentary drop to the 8.775-W initialization baseline rather than a sustained plateau. Subtracting the 7.6-W idle baseline, the total NPU-attributable energy obtained by integrating (P (t)− Pidle) over the two bursts is 23.31 J.

Fig. 2: System overview of the proposed progressive edge–cloud semantic communication framework. The edge encodes visual inputs into progressively refinable representations and transmits partial latent segments under bandwidth constraints. The cloud reconstructs the latent via a meta decoder and employs semantic quality-aware transmission control to adaptively request additional information until a target quality threshold is met, after which the LLM decoder generates the final output.
